id: title:jurajmajerik:accept a scalar value for in and not in property filters

review.posthog_relevance: Allows HogQL property filters created via the API with a scalar value to compile successfully, rather than raising an exception, by wrapping the scalar into a list before comparison. This supports stored filters that carry scalar values for IN/NOT IN operators.
review.reason: The change in P1.F1.H1 replaces a strict list-only check with a conditional that accepts a single scalar and converts it to a one-element list. This is a substantive, bounded correctness improvement: it prevents compilation failures for valid HogQL queries where stored filters carry scalar values for IN/NOT IN operators, while retaining the existing list-only path. No score is not;
review.uncertainty: The benefit relies on the existence of stored filters carrying scalar values, which is not independently verified in the provided context. The score assumes this use case exists and is relevant; without external adoption or incident data, this remains a potential rather than realized benefit.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains two hunks. P1.F1.H1 is a production implementation change. P1.F2.H1 is a test. I will provide observations for P1.F1.H1 as it represents the substantive change, while P1.F2.H1 is its supporting test. No score is assigned as requested.

observations.behavior: Replaces a strict list-only check with a conditional that accepts a single scalar and converts it to a one-element list, while retaining the list-only path. This allows IN/NOT IN operators to accept scalar values, treating them as one-element lists.
